fact.label: Recent incidents
fact.value: The status page lists 14 sandbox incidents from 6 August to 4 November 2026, nearly all in US-West-1; the longest was 4 hours 45 minutes of errors creating sandboxes from snapshots on 15 September.

Elevated error rates for sandbox operations

incidents.component: Template Builds in US-West-1, US-West-2, EU-West-1 and AP-Southeast-1 (widest in the window)

countBasis: All 14 incidents in /api/v2/incidents.json whose start falls between 6 August and 4 November 2026; the API holds every incident back to 15 June 2026, so the window is complete.

uptime.note: Region-level figures as shown on status.e2b.dev; the page also shows per-component figures (Sandbox Pause/Resume/Create, Sandbox Network Traffic, Persistent Volumes, Template Builds) per region.

method: Instatus JSON at https://status.e2b.dev/api/v2/incidents.json plus the rendered https://status.e2b.dev/ page for per-region uptime. Start and end are the earliest and latest display_at timestamps in each incident's updates (created_at is a backfill time for some records and can post-date the real start). Components and regions read from each incident page's 'Affected components' block.
gaps: The incidents API carries no component list, so regions/components were read from the individual incident pages.
Uptime figures are the page's rolling window ending 3 November 2026, one day short of the requested 4 November end date.

fact.label: Recent incidents
fact.value: Hetzner's status page publishes only its 15 most recent resolved entries, so it shows three outages affecting Cloud servers or their network between 28 October and 3 November 2026 rather than a full quarter; the longest was a 58-minute Cloud DNS API fault on 3 November.

source.quote: Fault report for Cloud DNS API and reverse DNS APIs (Primary IP, Floating IPs, Cloud Server, Load Balancer)

incidents.title: Fault report for Cloud DNS API and reverse DNS APIs (Primary IP, Floating IPs, Cloud Server, Load Balancer)
DHCP degraded in FSN1 and NBG1

countBasis: Outages (incidentType 'outage' or 'warning') affecting Cloud or the network of Cloud servers among the 15 resolved entries the page lists. The page also lists 11 planned-maintenance entries dated inside the window; those are not counted.
method: https://status.hetzner.com/ renders its incident list into the Next.js __NEXT_DATA__ payload; each of the 15 listed incidents was fetched from its /incident/<uuid> page for startTime, endTime, incidentType and affected system. The Atom feed at /en.atom carries announcements, not the incident history, and /api/v2/incidents.json returns 404.
gaps: The page shows a fixed list of the 15 most recent resolved entries (oldest 5 August 2026) with no archive or pagination, so a complete 6 August to 4 November count cannot be read. Everything between 6 August and 26 October is missing from the page.
The one entry dated 5 August (Outage of DENIC services) falls outside the window and is excluded.

fact.label: Recent incidents
fact.value: No VPS incident history is published: the status page has no VPS component group and exposes only its 50 most recent incidents (22 October to 4 November 2026), one of which, an emergency maintenance on server BOS-1335, was tagged to the Hostinger VPS API.

source.quote: This incident affected: Core Services (Hostinger VPS API).

incidents.title: Emergency Server BOS-1335 Maintenance
incidents.component: Core Services / Hostinger VPS API (server BOS-1335, United States)

countBasis: Not readable. The Statuspage API returns only the 50 most recent incidents (22 October to 4 November 2026) and the /history and /uptime pages render no incident list, so neither a 90-day count nor a VPS-only count can be established.

listedEntries.note: 43 of the 50 entries carry no component at all; the rest are tagged to hPanel, mail, agencies or a datacenter. The page's 97 components include no VPS group; the only VPS-labelled component is 'Hostinger VPS API'.

method: https://statuspage.hostinger.com/api/v2/incidents.json and /api/v2/components.json, plus the rendered /history, /history?page=1..2 and /uptime pages (all empty of incident data) and the individual incident page for the VPS-tagged entry.
gaps: 90-day incident count unavailable: the API caps at 50 records covering 13 days and the history page publishes no list.

Hostinger does not model VPS nodes or regions as status components, so VPS-affecting incidents cannot be separated from shared-hosting ones by component; most entries are per-server maintenance notices with no component tag.
The single 'Hostinger VPS API' tag is on a server maintenance notice whose text talks about 'client services hosted there', so the tag's meaning is uncertain.

fact.label: Recent incidents
fact.value: Akamai's status page lists 16 incidents touching compute, block or object storage or LKE from 6 August to 4 November 2026; the longest was a 34-hour Cloud Manager and API outage from 21 September that marked every region affected.

countBasis: Incidents whose affected components include a region (compute), Block Storage, Object Storage or Linode Kubernetes Engine. The page lists 28 incidents in the window in total; the other 12 are Cloud Manager-only, DNS, security advisories or platform notices with no compute/storage/LKE component.

listedEntries.note: The 50-record API reaches back to December 2025, so the window is complete.

method: Atlassian Statuspage JSON at https://status.linode.com/api/v2/incidents.json and /api/v2/components.json; /history?page=1..2 used as a cross-check on the incident list. Durations from started_at/resolved_at.
gaps: Two incidents in the set are still listed as 'monitoring' with no resolved_at: Block Storage (BR-GRU) opened 28 October and connectivity between ID-CGK and SG-SIN-2 opened 25 October, so no duration can be stated for them.

Postmortem-style entries can carry a started_at equal to the posting time; the 22 October LKE incident is such a case (its text gives an impact window of about 11:10-12:50 UTC). It is not among the three longest either way.
Security advisories with no affected component (CVE-2026-99999 PwnEscape, PHP RCE, F5/NGINX) are listed on the page but excluded from the 16.

fact.label: Recent incidents
fact.value: OVHcloud runs separate status pages: 18 VPS incidents and 72 Public Cloud incidents from 6 August to 4 November 2026. The longest VPS one left some VPS in the EU-SOUTH-LZ-MAD region unavailable for just over four days from 14 August.

[Global][Dedicated Servers/Virtual Private Servers] - Delivery incident notification
[EU-SOUTH-MIL][Containers & Orchestration] -  Managed Private Registry incident notification
incidents.component: Public Cloud / Managed Private Registry, EU-SOUTH-MIL

count.note: Two separate status pages. Counts exclude planned maintenance (impact 'maintenance' or titles starting '[Scheduled]').

countBasis: VPS: every non-maintenance entry on bare-metal-servers.status-ovhcloud.com whose title names Virtual Private Servers or VPS. Public Cloud: every non-maintenance entry on public-cloud.status-ovhcloud.com in the window (compute 18, storage 22, network 10, Public Cloud 8, containers/Kubernetes 6, AI/databases/analytics/identity 8).
method: Atlassian Statuspage history pages (/history?page=1..2) on public-cloud.status-ovhcloud.com and bare-metal-servers.status-ovhcloud.com; each page embeds a JSON blob with month-by-month incidents. Start and end times are taken from the 'Start time :'/'End time :' fields inside each incident's final message, not the list timestamp, which is the update-posting window (they differ by hours or weeks on long incidents).
gaps: VPS has no status page of its own: incidents appear on the Bare Metal Cloud page, filtered here by title. VPS incidents that do not name VPS in the title cannot be separated out.
The Public Cloud page mixes compute, storage, network, Kubernetes, AI, databases, analytics and identity services; the 72 is the whole page, not just compute.
OVHcloud's main status-ovhcloud.com page is a JavaScript shell with no incident data of its own, and vms.status-ovhcloud.com only shows per-datacenter real-time state, not incident history.
